title: Risk Governance in Public-Private Partnerships: An Analysis of Excessive Packaging Dimensions Based on Grounded Theory
content: Audits reveal that excessive packaging is a major cause of PPP project stagnation, yet its attributes and dimensions remain unclear. Clarifying these dimensions is critical for mitigating behavioral risks and advancing standardized operations. Applying constructivist grounded theory, the study builds a multidimensional framework for excessive packaging behavior in PPP projects, based on 220 valid samples collected through literature retrieval, web crawling, and interviews, and analyzed via iterative initial, focused, axial, and theoretical coding. Six core dimensions emerge: project expected returns, project entities, contract descriptions, project debt, financing structure, and project nature. The findings further identify two behavioral characteristics: prominent public-private stakeholder heterogeneity and phased differential distribution across the project lifecycle. The study completes the systematic dimension construction of excessive packaging as a behavioral risk, providing a diagnostic basis for the early identification of inflated and distorted project risk sources and for improving PPP risk resilience and governance efficiency.
